name: Majera
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Tourneux, Henry (2003), Majera material (cited on Glottolog for subclassification); Gravina (2014) Central Chadic comparative phonology
earlier_scan.note: Chadic sketch material exists but not reachable; no stress statement read

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page maje1243 (refs: Barreteau & Dieu 2000; Gravina 2014; Tourneux 2003; Campbell et al. 2022 ELCat).

Tourneux, Henry. 2018. Le syntagme de détermination nominale dans le parler « kotoko » de Mazéra (Cameroun). In D. Ibriszimow (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics IX (8th BICCL, Bayreuth 2016), 63-71. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. HAL halshs-02407734 (author version, 10 pp., scanned; scanned here).
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. The only published first-hand description of Mazera; data are tone-marked and tone is grammatically contrastive (plural 'par changement tonal': yàzè/yazé 'homme', gàndè/gandé 'pierre'; 'modifications tonales tant du déterminé que du déterminant', author-version pp. 4, 9). Sections: localisation, genre, nombre, détermination, phénomènes morphonologiques.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic. LOT 375. Utrecht: LOT. Sec. 8.2.3 Mazera, p. 212.
sources.note: p. 212: 'For Mazera there is nothing published on the language, and the only data available is a list of 350 words (Allison n.d.). The data is consistent with the tentative analysis described for Zina.' Reconstruction explicitly excludes tone and stress; no stress statement for Mazera.

sources.citation: Allison, Sean D. 2012. Aspects of a Grammar of Makary Kotoko. PhD dissertation, University of Colorado.
sources.note: Describes Mpade (Makary), not Majera; Mazera appears only in the Kotoko classification table. Nothing on Majera stress.

sources.citation: Barreteau, Daniel & Michel Dieu. 2005 [2000]. Linguistique. In C. Seignobos & O. Iyébi-Mandjek (eds), Atlas de la province Extrême-Nord Cameroun, planche 11. Paris: IRD Éditions (OpenEdition Books 11562).
sources.note: Classification and localisation only: 'le majəra est parlé autour de Mazera... Trois parlers très proches : majəra proprement dit, ulo-kajire, hwalam.' Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2001 [publ. 2003]. Le système consonantique des langues dites « kotoko ». In E. Wolff (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics [I], 115-135. Köln: Köppe. HAL halshs-00349309.
sources.note: Gives the Mazéra /majra/ consonant chart (sec. 2.C.a) and tone-marked Mazéra cognates throughout; segmental only, no statement on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2000 [publ. 2003]. Le système vocalique dans le groupe « kotoko ». In K. Lébikaza (ed.), Actes du 3e Congrès mondial de linguistique africaine, Lomé 2000, 69-77. Köln: Köppe. HAL halshs-00349308.
sources.note: Vowel systems only; 'Le parler de Mazéra est justiciable en synchronie d'une analyse analogue à celle que l'on vient de faire pour Zina' (two full vowel phonemes). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Bagley, R. Kelly & James Roberts. 1991. Kotoko Survey Report. Yaoundé: SIL / MESIRES-CREA. 64 pp. (image-only PDF from silcam.org via Wayback; pp. 1-4 scanned).
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey (lexicostatistics, RTT, questionnaires); Mazera ('Madgica', ALCAM majera) is one test site. Table of contents has no phonology; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Allison, Sean. 2020. A Grammar of Makary Kotoko (Grammars and Sketches of the World's Languages). Leiden: Brill. Ch. 'Comparison' (DOI 10.1163/9789004422674_021).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; Harvard e-access not checked
sources.note: Comparative chapter across Kotoko lects by the collector of the Mazera wordlist; could include Mazera forms with prosodic marking. Describes Mpade, not Majera, so at best incidental.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2007. L'inversion tonale en kotoko. In H. Tourneux (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics IV: Comparative and Descriptive Studies, Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. (HAL halshs-00327623, no file)
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Tourneux's only dedicated prosody paper on the Kotoko group; if any Kotoko-wide remark on tone vs. accent (including Kotoko-South Zina/Mazera) exists in print, it is here.

sources.citation: Odden, David. 2002-2007. Papers on Zina Kotoko tone (e.g. 'The verbal tone system of Zina', 'Consonant-tone interaction in Zina') in Schmidt, Odden & Holmberg (eds) 2002, Some Aspects of the Grammar of Zina Kotoko (LINCOM) and later articles.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Zina (jina1244) is Majera's only close sister (Kotoko South); Odden's tonal analyses are the nearest proxy for the prosodic type, but they do not describe Majera and cannot be entered for maje1243.

sources.citation: Tourneux, Henry. 2000. La formation du pluriel en kotoko. In H. E. Wolff & O. Gensler (eds), Proceedings of the 2nd World Congress of African Linguistics, Leipzig 1997, 747-761. Köln: Köppe.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Cited in Tourneux 2018 as the group-wide treatment of plural formation incl. tonal plurals; may contain a short note on Mazera prosody/transcription conventions.

sources.citation: Allison, Sean. n.d. Mazera word list (c. 350 items). Unpublished, SIL Cameroon (cited as the only Mazera data in Gravina 2014:212).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Only other primary Mazera data set known; an SIL wordlist may carry tone/stress marking or a transcription note, though a stress statement is unlikely.
